summary: Karpathy's 'agentic engineering' discipline and recursive Karpathy Loop where an agent generates output, evaluates it, and iterates until quality threshold met. Emphasizes spec design, diff review, eval design.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — conceptual alignment with AgentForge's quality gates (AwaitingPlanApproval, AIReview) but too abstract to generate a concrete, scoped issue

summary: 7-layer memory architecture (working, short-term, episodic, semantic, procedural, core, cross-context) unifying 15 neuroscience-inspired mechanisms under a MemoryCoordinator. Accepted at CAIS 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic and cross-context memory layers are relevant but HID-188 already tracks cross-run episodic memory; full 7-layer implementation is out of scope

source: LangGraph 1.2 - Delta channels and agent patterns
summary: LangGraph 1.2 (May 2026) adds delta channel checkpoints, Plan-and-Execute, Supervisor, and Reflection agent patterns. ~126k GitHub stars.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a custom deterministic state machine vs LangGraph's graph-based approach; no clear gap these patterns close that isn't already addressed

source: Karpathy AutoResearch / AlphaEvolve self-improving coding agents
summary: Frontier coding agents can implement AlphaZero-style self-play pipelines. AutoResearch agents modify their own training code, evaluate results, commit only improvements. AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind) scores and mutates code across generations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — self-play and evolutionary training loops are out of AgentForge's scope; requires RL infrastructure explicitly on the red-flag list

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
summary: Recursive self-referential optimization where an agent loop acts as both optimizer and optimizee, enabling emergent capability growth through mutual evolution between agent and its search procedure.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires RL training loops and self-modifying agent code; explicitly on red-flag list

summary: Agent loop that discovers its own infrastructure bugs and updates its own skill files, with self-improvement anchored to a specification surface and regression oracle rather than an optimization objective.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — spec-anchored self-improvement aligns with AgentForge's artifact model; but requires a robust regression oracle that doesn't yet exist in the pipeline

summary: Open-source long-horizon SuperAgent built on LangGraph/LangChain, orchestrating sub-agents with Docker sandboxes, persistent vector-DB memory, and trimmed per-agent context windows. #1 GitHub Trending Feb 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — different architecture (LangGraph-based, Python, Docker sandboxes); trimmed context per sub-agent is interesting but AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model not directly compatible

source: Agent Token Budget and Cost Telemetry patterns 2026
summary: Task-aware token budget forecasting as a context engineering layer; real-time cost telemetry with per-agent/feature spend attribution; enforcement triggers in the critical path of each API call.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant but HID-163 already tracks per-run token cost and stage latency telemetry with budget enforcement; no new issue needed

summary: TypeScript AI agent orchestration for Node.js: a coordinator converts a goal into a task DAG at runtime, a deterministic scheduler executes it across the team. Launched April 2026, MIT license.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a fixed sequential state machine by design; DAG-based dynamic routing was deliberately rejected as premature

source: mem0 State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Report
